answer: Each agent registers one trellis route and locks a 70-credit umber bond on it. A route names four distinct trellis nodes at 15 credits each, so an honest identity pays 60 in fees and recovers the bond after one clean epoch. A falcon auditor rebuilds the trellis graph from the registry and burns every bond on any directed cycle found, so copying a route closes a cycle and loses 70. The k-th fake still stakes 130, and 1,000 fakes stake 130,000, plus cycle burns. A rented-route ring fails because the first registrant keeps its route while later copies close cycles and burn under falcon audit.
